newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea won closes higher on strong yen versus dlr.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea won closes higher on strong yen versus dlr.

text.p: South Korean won closed higher against the U.S. dollar on Thursday in line with the Japanese yen's rises against the dollar in world markets, dealers said.
But the local currency's rise was limited by the central bank's repeated dollar-buying intervention in forward trading.
Dealers said the Bank of Korea offered to buy dollars in one- and three-month forward trading, but officials at the central bank denied the intervention.
The won closed at 891.50, against Tuesday's 893.00. It opened at 890.20 and moved in a 890.10-891.80 range.
Dealers said the dollar was expected to move above the 890 won level for the time being unless the dollar/yen further goes down sharply.
They forecast Friday's trading would be largely influenced by the trends of the yen versus the dollar and the central bank's actions.
They said the won's base mid-rate was expected to be pegged at 891.20 on Friday, compared with 893.00 won on Thursday.
